claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me ask you the first question:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

To help me navigate the eligibility rules correctly, could you tell me:
1. The name(s) of your child/children
2. Their age(s)

This information will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 13 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. I'm assessing eligibility for **Alex, who is 13 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, let me navigate to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 13, most of the basic requirements are already met. Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

This is just to confirm he doesn't have full-time employment, which could affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 13, so he's still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - Alex doesn't work and is in school. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(This is a standard check - most school-age children won't be receiving these, but I need to confirm for Alex.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular school kid.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's 13 and in school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's too young for that - he's just in regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's what I expected. Let me move forward to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK?** 

Or if you don't normally live in the UK, do you have any of the following circumstances:
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with specific conditions like working, job-seeking, studying, or having sufficient resources)
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

For most people, the answer is simply "yes, I normally live in the UK" - could you confirm your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you're living abroad, I need to check if you still qualify under any of the special circumstances.

**Can you tell me more about your situation abroad? Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**
2. **Do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** (If yes, I'll need to ask follow-up questions about whether you're working, job-seeking, studying, or have sufficient resources)
3. **Are you a Crown servant living abroad** (e.g., diplomat, military personnel in qualifying countries)?
4. **Or is your situation different from these options?**

This will help me determine if you can still qualify for Child Benefit despite living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply to me. I'm just living abroad - I don't have settled or pre-settled status, and I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Based on the information you've provided, I need to let you know the outcome of this assessment.

Since you don't normally live in the UK and don't meet any of the special residency circumstances (settled status, pre-settled status, or Crown servant status), you unfortunately would not be eligible for Child Benefit under the residency requirements.

Let me confirm this outcome with the formal decision:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

**Result: NOT ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Why:**
While Alex is a perfectly qualifying child (he's 13, in school, not working full-time, and has no disqualifying factors), you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit because you don't meet the residency requirements.

**The Rule:**
To claim Child Benefit in the UK, you must normally live in the UK, OR meet one of the following special circumstances:
- Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with additional conditions like working or studying)
- Be a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Since you live abroad without any of these special circumstances, you cannot claim Child Benefit.

**What You Can Do:**
If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you return to live in the UK), you may become eligible at that point. You can always contact HMRC to discuss your specific situation further:
- **Phone:** 0300 200 3100
- **Website:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit eligibility?

reasonings: Alex is 13 years old and meets the basic age requirement for Child Benefit. He is not working full-time, does not receive benefits in his own right, and is not in an apprenticeship - all of which would normally make him a qualifying child. However, the claimant does not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant lives abroad and does not have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, pre-settled status, or any Crown servant status that would allow them to claim while living outside the UK. According to Child Benefit eligibility rules, the claimant must normally live in the UK or meet special circumstances to be eligible. Without meeting these residency requirements, the claimant cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Child Benefit requires that the claimant normally lives in the UK, or meets specific special circumstances (such as EU Settlement Scheme status or Crown servant status abroad). The claimant lives abroad without any of these qualifying circumstances, which makes them ineligible to claim Child Benefit."
